I'll think through this year the way I always do — looking at what we did last year and what my neighbors are doing.

---

My 8.2 mu is split up. About 2 mu I plant cotton — it's on the piece near the road where the soil is a little sandy, cotton does alright there. The other 6.2 mu I do wheat in winter, then maize right after wheat comes off in June. That's how everyone around here farms.

**For my wheat (6.2 mu):**
Last October I already put the seed in the ground, so it's growing now. This spring when the ground thaws and the wheat turns green again, I need to put urea down. I use about one bag (50 jin, so 25 kg) of urea per mu when I topdress — that's what my husband's brother does and his wheat always looks good. Before sowing I put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu — the kind the shopkeeper at the crossroads sells, 15-15-15. I water the wheat maybe 3 or 4 times — once before winter so it doesn't freeze, once when it greens up, once when it's jointing, and once when the grain is filling. If the rain comes I skip one. I spray against aphids and the yellow rust maybe 2 times. I use the improved seed from the shop, not old seed. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, I hope for the same.

**For my maize (6.2 mu, after wheat):**
When wheat comes off in June I don't plough, I just use the seed-drill that goes right into the stubble — the machine owner charges 30 yuan per mu. Cheaper and the ground stays wet. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the shopkeeper recommends that year. I put compound fertilizer with the seed, about one and a half bags per mu, then when the maize is knee-high I put urea, about one bag per mu. I water once or twice if July and August are dry — my well is close. I spray once for the borer worm. Last year I got about 1100 jin per mu.

**For my cotton (2 mu):**
Cotton is more trouble. I plough the land properly before planting in April. I use Bt cotton seed — the kind that doesn't get eaten so much by the bollworm, everyone uses it now. I put two bags compound fertilizer per mu before planting, then urea at flowering, about 30 jin per mu. Cotton needs potash more than wheat does, so I look for a compound with more K. I water 3 times. I spray more on cotton — maybe 5 times for aphids, spider mites, and whatever else comes. Picking is done by me and my daughter-in-law when she's home. Last year I got about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I don't like to save on fertilizer. If I skip a bag and the yield drops, that's much worse than spending the extra 150 yuan. Wheat and maize are for eating and selling a little; cotton is for cash.
